dm: Blessed One, how should those who have correctly entered the bodhisattva vehicle abide?
gm: Blessed One, how should those who have correctly entered the bodhisattva vehicle dwell?

dm: How should they practice?
gm: How should they practice?

dm: How should the mind be held?
gm: How should they fully control their minds?

dm: When he had spoken thus, the Blessed One addressed the venerable Subhūti in this way:
gm: When he had said this, the Blessed One said this to the venerable Subhūti:

dm: Subhūti, in this regard, one who has correctly entered the bodhisattva vehicle should think thus: "I shall lead all sentient beings to final nirvāṇa in the realm of nirvāṇa without remainder."
gm: Subhūti, here one who has correctly entered the bodhisattva vehicle should think thus: 'I will lead all sentient beings to complete nirvāṇa in the realm of nirvāṇa without remainder of the aggregates.

dm: Even though immeasurable sentient beings are led to final nirvāṇa in this way, one should generate the mind with the thought that not even one sentient being has been led to final nirvāṇa.
gm: Even though immeasurable sentient beings have been led to complete nirvāṇa in this way, no sentient being whatsoever has been led to complete nirvāṇa'—thus should they generate the mind.

dm: Why is that? Subhūti, if a bodhisattva engages in the perception of a sentient being, they should not be called a bodhisattva;
gm: Why is that? Subhūti, if a bodhisattva engages in the perception of a sentient being, they are not to be called a bodhisattva,

dm: and if they engage in the perception of a person, they should not be called a bodhisattva.
gm: and even if they engage in a perception up to that of a person, it is because they are not to be called a bodhisattva.

dm: Why is that? Subhūti, it is because there is no phenomenon whatsoever that can be called "having correctly entered the bodhisattva vehicle."
gm: Why is that? Subhūti, it is because there is no dharma whatsoever called 'one who has correctly entered the bodhisattva vehicle'.

dm: Subhūti, what do you think?
gm: Subhūti, what do you think?

dm: Do you think that there is any phenomenon whatsoever that the Tathāgata has fully realized as unsurpassed, perfectly complete enlightenment from the Tathāgata Dīpaṃkara?
gm: Do you think there is any dharma whatsoever by which the Tathāgata fully awakened to unsurpassable, perfectly complete awakening from the Tathāgata Dīpaṃkara?

dm: When he had spoken those words, the venerable Subhūti addressed the Blessed One as follows:
gm: When he had said this, the venerable Subhūti said this to the Blessed One:

dm: Blessed One, there is no phenomenon whatsoever that the Tathāgata has fully realized as unsurpassed, perfectly complete enlightenment from the Tathāgata Dīpaṃkara.
gm: Blessed One, there is no dharma whatsoever by which the Tathāgata fully awakened to unsurpassable, perfectly complete awakening from the Tathāgata Dīpaṃkara.

dm: When he had spoken thus, the Blessed One addressed the venerable Subhūti in this way:
gm: When he had said this, the Blessed One said this to the venerable Subhūti:

dm: Subhūti, it is so. It is just so.
gm: Subhūti, it is so, it is so.

dm: There is no phenomenon whatsoever that the Tathāgata has fully realized as unsurpassed, perfectly complete enlightenment from the Tathāgata Dīpaṃkara.
gm: There is no dharma whatsoever by which the Tathāgata fully awakened to unsurpassable, perfectly complete awakening from the Tathāgata Dīpaṃkara.

dm: Subhūti, if there were any phenomenon that the Tathāgata had fully realized as enlightenment, the Tathāgata Dīpaṃkara would not have given me the prophecy, saying, "Young Brahmin, in a future time, you will become the Tathāgata, Arhat, Perfectly Complete Buddha named Śākyamuni."
gm: Subhūti, if there had been some dharma by which the Tathāgata fully awakened, the Tathāgata Dīpaṃkara would not have prophesied to me, 'Brahmin boy, in a future time you will become a tathāgata, an arhat, a perfectly complete buddha named Śākyamuni.'

dm: Subhūti, because there is no phenomenon whatsoever that the Tathāgata has fully realized as unsurpassed, perfectly complete enlightenment,
gm: Subhūti, since there is no dharma whatsoever by which the Tathāgata fully awakened to unsurpassable, perfectly complete awakening,

dm: for that reason, the Tathāgata Dīpaṃkara prophesied to me, "Young Brahmin, in a future time, you will become the Tathāgata, Arhat, Perfectly Complete Buddha named Śākyamuni."
gm: therefore the Tathāgata Dīpaṃkara prophesied to me, 'Brahmin boy, in a future time you will become a tathāgata, an arhat, a perfectly complete buddha named Śākyamuni.'

dm: Why is that? Subhūti, because the term "Tathāgata" is a designation for the true suchness.
gm: Why is that? Subhūti, 'Tathāgata' is a designation for true suchness.

dm: Furthermore, Subhūti, if anyone were to say that the Tathāgata, the Arhat, the perfectly complete Buddha, has fully awakened to unsurpassed, perfectly complete enlightenment, that person is speaking falsely.
gm: Furthermore, Subhūti, if anyone were to speak thus: 'The Tathāgata, the arhat, the perfectly complete buddha fully awakened to unsurpassable, perfectly complete awakening,' he would be speaking falsely.

dm: The Tathāgata speaks of them as "bodhisattvas," calling them "bodhisattvas."
gm: That one is called 'a bodhisattva, a bodhisattva' by the Tathāgata.

dm: Why is that? Subhūti, because there is no phenomenon whatsoever that the Tathāgata has fully awakened to as unsurpassed, perfectly complete enlightenment.
gm: Why is that? Subhūti, it is because there is no dharma whatsoever by which the Tathāgata fully awakened to unsurpassable, perfectly complete awakening.

dm: Subhūti, regarding the phenomena that the Tathāgata has fully awakened to, or what he has taught, there is neither truth nor falsehood.
gm: Subhūti, in the dharma that the Tathāgata fully awakened to or taught, there is neither truth nor falsehood.

dm: Therefore, the Tathāgata has declared that all phenomena are the qualities of a Buddha.
gm: Therefore, the Tathāgata has taught that all dharmas are the Buddha's dharmas.

dm: Subhūti, what are called "all phenomena" are all non-phenomena.
gm: Subhūti, as for what is called 'all dharmas,' they are all non-dharmas.

dm: Therefore, all phenomena are called the qualities of a Buddha.
gm: Therefore, all dharmas are called the Buddha's dharmas.

dm: Subhūti, it is like this: for example, a person who possesses a human body and has become a great body.
gm: Subhūti, it is like, for example, a person endowed with a human body who has a large body.

dm: The venerable Subhūti replied, "Blessed One, that which the Tathāgata has spoken of as a person possessing a human body and a great body, the Tathāgata has spoken of as having no body."
gm: Venerable Subhūti said, "Blessed One, as for what the Tathāgata has taught as 'a person endowed with a human body and having a large body', the Tathāgata has taught that as being without a body.

dm: Therefore, it is called possessing a body and a great body.
gm: Therefore, it is called 'endowed with a body and having a large body'."

dm: The Blessed One replied, "Subhūti, it is so. It is just so.
gm: The Blessed One said, "Subhūti, so it is. So it is.

dm: If a bodhisattva were to say, 'I shall lead sentient beings to complete nirvana,' that one should not be called a bodhisattva.
gm: If any bodhisattva were to speak thus: 'I shall cause sentient beings to completely pass into nirvāṇa,' he would not be called a bodhisattva.

dm: Why is that? Subhūti, do you think that there is any phenomenon called a bodhisattva?
gm: Why is that? Subhūti, do you think there is any dharma whatsoever called 'bodhisattva'?"

dm: Subhūti replied, "No, Blessed One, it is not."
gm: Subhūti said, "Blessed One, that is not so."

dm: The Blessed One replied, "Subhūti, therefore the Tathāgata has said that all phenomena are without sentient beings, without life, and without persons."
gm: The Blessed One said, "Subhūti, therefore, the Tathāgata has taught that all dharmas are without a sentient being, without a soul, without a person."

dm: Furthermore, Subhūti, if a bodhisattva were to say, "I shall accomplish the arrays of buddhafields," that should also be spoken of in that same way.
gm: Moreover, Subhūti, if any bodhisattva were to speak thus: 'I shall accomplish the arrays of the fields,' he too would be spoken of in the same way.

dm: Why is that? Subhūti, the so-called "arrays of buddhafields, arrays of buddhafields"—the Tathāgata has said that they are not arrays.
gm: Why is that? Subhūti, as for what is called 'arrays of the fields, arrays of the fields', the Tathāgata has taught them as being without array.

dm: Therefore, they are called "arrays of buddhafields."
gm: Therefore, they are called 'arrays of the fields'.

dm: Subhūti, any bodhisattva who is convinced that "phenomena are selfless, phenomena are selfless," is called a bodhisattva mahāsattva by the Tathāgata, the Arhat, the perfectly complete Buddha.
gm: Subhūti, as for any bodhisattva who resolutely believes thus: 'dharmas are without self, dharmas are without self,' the Tathāgata, the Arhat, the Perfectly Complete Buddha calls him a 'bodhisattva, a great being'.
